chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, and from another, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Allah is Great and Exalted. The servants are not able to describe Him, nor do they attain the reality of His greatness.
Visions do not comprehend Him, while He comprehends visions, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

And He is not described by 'how', nor by 'where', nor by location. How could I describe Him by 'how', when He is the One who originated the 'how' until it came to be 'how'? Thus 'how' came to be known only through what He originated for us of 'how'.
Or how could I describe Him by 'where', when He is the One who originated the 'where' until it came to be 'where'? Thus 'where' came to be known only through what He originated for us of 'where'.
Or how could I describe Him by location, when He is the One who originated location until it came to be location? Thus location came to be known only through what He originated for us of location.

So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is within every place and outside every thing. Visions do not comprehend Him, while He comprehends visions. There is no god except Him, the Most High, the Magnificent, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

key_terms.اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ: the One subtle beyond perception and fully aware of all things
key_terms.الْأَبْصَارُ: visions or sights of created beings
key_terms.بِأَيْنٍ: by place or by asking 'where' about Him
key_terms.بِحَيْثٍ: by spatial location or situational placement
key_terms.بِكَيْفٍ: by modality or by asking 'how' about His being
key_terms.رَفِيعٌ: lofty and exalted above all created limitations
key_terms.عَظِيمٌ: immensely great beyond the full grasp of creation
key_terms.كُنْهَ: the true reality or ultimate depth of something

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explain that Allah cannot be described by how or where?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the transcendence and incomparability of Allah, teaching that created categories such as modality, place, and location cannot be applied to Him. It emphasizes that Allah is known through what He has made known, while human perception and description remain incapable of grasping the reality of His essence.
